about.title: I turn AI research into things people can actually use.
paragraphs: I'm a final-year Information Systems undergraduate at UiTM Shah Alam, specialising in AI and full-stack development. I build and deploy computer vision, LLM/RAG and agentic AI systems with Python, FastAPI, React.js and Docker, and I like taking them all the way to real hardware: Raspberry Pi edge devices, sensors and live demos in front of judges.

I lead AISe, a national-level AI infrastructure project, and I've won three Gold Awards (NISMEC 2026, iREx 2024, i-SIIDEC 2024). Outside the code I design and organise: media teams, promotions and contingent logistics for university-wide tournaments.
I'm looking for a software engineering or AI engineering role where I can ship things people use.

projects.title: AISe
projects.subtitle: Intelligent Infrastructure Management Platform
projects.summary: An AI platform that detects potholes and road cracks from images, then turns detections into inspection reports, automated alerts and a chatbot that answers questions about past reports.
bullets: Led team Half Genius, one of two UiTM teams selected for Maker-Preneur National 2026, while building the application and system and coordinating the team's workstreams.
Detects potholes and road cracks with a trained YOLOv8 computer vision model, served by a FastAPI backend with a React.js interface.
Integrated an LLM to generate inspection summaries and reports and send automated alerts via email and Telegram, plus a RAG-based chatbot for querying reports.
Ran the prototype on edge hardware (Raspberry Pi 5, Hailo AI accelerator, AI camera); pitched to judges and presented to the Deputy Secretary-General (Policy), Ministry of Higher Education.

stories.title: From a Raspberry Pi to the Deputy Secretary-General
stories.excerpt: How a pothole detector grew into a full AI platform and ended up in front of a government minister's office.
body: AISe is an AI platform that detects potholes and road cracks from images using a trained YOLOv8 model, with a FastAPI backend and a React.js interface. On top of detection, an LLM writes the inspection summaries, sends alerts by email and Telegram, and a RAG chatbot answers questions about past reports.

As team lead of Half Genius, I coordinated the team's workstreams while building the application and the system itself. Our team was one of only two UiTM teams selected for Maker-Preneur National 2026.

The prototype ran on edge hardware: a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo AI accelerator and an AI camera. We pitched it to the judges and presented it to the Deputy Secretary-General (Policy) of the Ministry of Higher Education.

stories.title: Three Gold Awards, one habit: ship the demo
stories.excerpt: iREx 2024, i-SIIDEC 2024 and NISMEC 2026, plus the placements in between.
body: In 2024 I won Gold at the International Industrial Revolution 4.0 Exhibition (iREx) in May, followed by Gold at the International Student Invention Innovation Development Exhibition Competition (i-SIIDEC) in August. In 2026 I added a third Gold at the National Innovation & Sustainability Melati Challenge (NISMEC).

Alongside those: 2nd place overall at the UiTM Kedah Youth Innovation Competition (Jul 2024), 3rd place at YES! MyNext Move 2025 organised by TalentCorp, Top 20 at ProSolve National 2025, and 3rd place in the ProCode competitive programming workshop (Dec 2025).

stories.title: The glove that talks back
stories.excerpt: A wearable that streams sensor data to a local Gemma 3 model and gets coached back in plain language.
body: The AI-Powered Smart Wrist System was an IoT wearable glove built for the ITT569 course, using an Arduino Nano, an ESP32, an MPU6050 motion sensor and a MAX30100 pulse sensor.

My part was the AI layer and the FastAPI backend, hosting a local Gemma 3 (1B) model that turns real-time sensor data into trend analysis, exercise summaries and recommendations, plus a React.js interface for historical records.
I also mentored the networking team on AI architecture and prompt engineering, and the lecturer recognised the project as one of the best in the class.

stories.title: From diploma to Dean's List
stories.excerpt: Kedah to Shah Alam, a full-stack internship in between, and a CGPA that kept climbing.
body: I started with a Diploma in Computer Science at UiTM Kedah (Oct 2022 – Feb 2025), finishing with a CGPA of 3.53.
Between Sep 2024 and Feb 2025 I worked as a Full Stack Intern at Asrix Prime Berhad, testing LLMs, RAG pipelines and AI agents, and building FastAPI services and React.js interfaces.
In March 2025 I moved on to the BSc (Hons.) in Information Systems Engineering (Big Data Track) at UiTM Shah Alam. My CGPA is now 3.65, and I made the Dean's List for the Oct 2025 – Feb 2026 session.

stories.title: Leading beyond the code
stories.excerpt: 2,000+ attendees, a 58-agency tournament and 300+ graphic assets.
body: As Head of Promotion for the Karnival Sukan Varsiti Komuniti UiTM Shah Alam, I led promotions with Al-Ikhsan Sport and attracted 2,000+ attendees on opening day.
On the contingent secretariat for SUKANUN 2025 I managed accreditation, accommodation and athlete logistics across a 58-agency tournament, and our contingent placed 3rd overall.
As a media team volunteer for UiTM in April 2026, I produced 300+ graphic assets for a 3-day national-level tournament.

bullets: Tested and evaluated Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines and AI agents for real-world use cases, and benchmarked GPU and CPU performance for AI workloads.
Integrated image generation tools (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E) and researched ERP/CRM systems with Docker-based deployment.
Built backend services with FastAPI and user interfaces with React.js in a Linux environment, using GitHub for version control and team collaboration.
